+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M1MNWW4P14DK407XYSF22SMX
+- 01M1MNXY19R8HPEMNGF2WXB0G6
+- 01M1MP01P7SV7C2S0S8QZ0A60T
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8980'
+title: Download progress on stderr, and the verbose and quiet rules
+---
+## What
+
+cli-plan.md §5.7. The default profile is large, and nothing is on disk
+on a clean machine, so the first `acp-agent run "hello"` downloads
+gigabytes. A person who asks for a haiku and gets a silent terminal for
+ten minutes will conclude that the tool is broken. **Progress is not
+decoration here. It is the difference between working and appearing
+hung.**
+
+Router already does the work. `ResolutionProgress` carries the `phase`
+(`sizing`, `downloading`, `loading`, `ready`, `failed`), a `fraction`,
+and per-slot `bytesDownloaded` and `bytesTotal`, and
+`RoutedACPAgent.init` already takes `reporting: ResolutionProgress?`.
+This task passes one in and renders it.
+
+In `Sources/acp-agent/ProgressReporter.swift`, with the renderer the
+terminal spike chose:
+
+| Condition | stderr shows |
+|---|---|
+| stderr is a terminal | The phase, the slot, and a bar with the bytes. Then the running tool name on one line, rewritten in place. |
+| stderr is a pipe or a file | Nothing, until something fails. |
+| `--verbose` | The session events, one line each: the tool calls, the plan updates, the stop reason. In a pipe too. |
+| `--quiet` | Nothing but errors, in a terminal too. |
+
+The bar is drawn only for the resolution, and it is erased when the
+first answer chunk arrives. Nothing here touches stdout, so the §5.6
+byte-exact rule holds in every case.
+
+- [ ] Pass a `ResolutionProgress` into the agent construction
+- [ ] Render the phase, the slot and the bar, on stderr only
+- [ ] Erase the bar at the first answer chunk
+- [ ] `--verbose` and `--quiet`
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] With stderr a terminal, a resolution draws a bar that advances.
+- [ ] With stderr a pipe, a successful default run writes zero bytes to
+      stderr.
+- [ ] `--verbose` writes one line per session event, in a pipe too.
+- [ ] `--quiet` writes nothing but errors, in a terminal too.
+- [ ] stdout is unchanged in every case.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/ProgressReporterTests.swift`:
+      a scripted `ResolutionProgress` is advanced through `sizing`,
+      `downloading` and `ready`; the reporter's output holds the byte
+      counts, and it goes to the injected stderr handle only.
+- [ ] With a non-terminal destination the reporter writes zero bytes.
+- [ ] An integration test asserts that the bar never appears on stdout,
+      whatever the progress values.
+- [ ] `--verbose` and `--quiet` each get one test.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes.
+
+## Blocked by
+
+The Router change (`ResolutionProgress.fraction` and `.slots` public).
+Without it this task cannot read the numbers it must draw.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m21zafp7a6w81d0xvewqhq3v
+  text: |-
+    Research, measured in the real sources.
+
+    Router `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Resolution/ResolutionProgress.swift` at the pinned revision:
+    - `ResolutionProgress` is `@MainActor @Observable public final class`. `phase` is `public var` (a consumer can write it). `fraction` and `slots` are `public internal(set)`.
+    - `SlotProgress` is public, but its `init` is internal. A test outside Router CANNOT build one, so a test cannot put byte counts into a real `ResolutionProgress.slots`.
+    - `phases` yields only on a phase change, so it misses the byte counts that move inside `downloading`. The reporter must poll.
+    - `ModelSlot` is a `String` enum with `standard`, `flash`, `embedding`. It is not `CaseIterable`, so the reporter orders slots by raw value for a stable pick.
+
+    Consequence for the card's tests: the reporter reads through a small protocol seam in this repository, `ResolutionProgressReading`, with one `@MainActor` snapshot property. `ResolutionProgress` gets the production conformance here; the test drives a scripted conformance through `sizing`, `downloading` and `ready` with byte counts. That is the only way to script byte counts, because `SlotProgress.init` is internal.
+
+    `TerminalRenderer.progressBar` draws one fixed message for every report, so the phase and the slot cannot change while the bar runs. The report closure takes the line text as well, so each redraw names the phase and the slot.
+
+    `RoutedACPAgent.init` resolves the profile inside `init`, so the poll task starts before that `await` and is cancelled after it. `AgentComposition.compose` takes the progress object, and `RunCommand` makes it before the composition.
+  timestamp: 2026-09-09T02:18:02.823580+00:00

+    - evidence: 7 files — Sources/acp-agent/ProgressReporter.swift (new), Sources/acp-agent/Terminal/TerminalRenderer.swift, Sources/acp-agent/AgentComposition.swift, Sources/acp-agent/RunCommand.swift, Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/ProgressReporterTests.swift (new), Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/TerminalRendererTests.swift, Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/EventLineWriterTests.swift
+    - `swift test`: 516 tests in 54 suites pass, 1 known issue. The baseline was 511 in 53 suites, so this card adds 5 tests and one suite, and breaks nothing.
+
+    What the design decided, and why:
+
+    - `TerminalRenderer.progressBar` drew one fixed message for every report, so a bar could not name the phase or the slot that changes while it runs. The report closure now takes the line text as its first argument. Three call sites in the two older suites changed with the signature.

+    - The bar is erased when the composition returns. That is before the wire opens, so it is before the first answer chunk.
+
+    Two things a later agent should know:
+
+    - `RunCommandTests.onlyTheCompositionNamesTheAgentType` fails when any other file under `Sources/acp-agent/` writes the agent type name, a doc comment included. The first version of the two new comments named it and the test went red; the comments now say "the construction of the agent".
